newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bremen cotton consumers lack nearby cover.
newsitem.headline: Bremen cotton consumers lack nearby cover.

text.p: German cotton consumers are insufficiently supplied for the near future, a fortnightly market report from the Bremen Cotton Exchange said on Monday.
It reported heavy turnover in Central Asian standard 1-3 and West African material although consumers were complaining about the high level of shippers prices.
These transactions were for spot dates through first quarter 1998.
Other deals included Argentine cotton, Mexico-Juarez and Syrian medium grades for spot or second quarter.
Sales from local stocks were reported in Central Asian, Malian, Syrian and Sudanese cotton varieties.
Cotton stocks as of March 21 totalled 39,506 bales, down from 40,589 a fortnight earlier and well below the 116,287 recorded a year earlier.
In the long staple sector, the Exchange reported trades in Egyptian Giza 70/75/77 and Central Asian lower grades as well as Israel Pima, all for 1997.
